input.quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 13 binds Clear Capital with a non-solicit. It already meets most of the fallback: it is mutual, runs only 12 months (well inside the 24-month walk-away line), is limited to personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, and is a solicitation restriction rather than a prohibited no-hire. It fails the fallback on one material term, however: there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches, which the rule summary treats as a condition of acceptability ("only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out"). As drafted, an untargeted job posting answered by a RadialSpark engineer could put us in breach. We therefore propose the minimal fallback edit — a single carve-out sentence for untargeted solicitations and unsolicited approaches — rather than the preferred position (no non-solicit at all), which would be disproportionate given the clause is mutual and otherwise narrow. Separately noted but not flagged: the 12 months runs from termination of the Agreement rather than from the end of the individual's involvement, a minor variance from the preferred formulation.

proposal.summary: Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs to the mutual non-solicit.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added the customary carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches so that neither party breaches this section merely by running an untargeted job posting or hiring someone who approaches it on their own initiative. The rest of the clause (mutual, 12 months, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, no no-hire) is acceptable to us as drafted.

ops.oldText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
ops.newText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this Section shall restrict either party from (a) making general solicitations for employment or engagement that are not specifically directed at the other party's personnel (including advertisements, job postings and searches by recruiting firms not targeted at such personnel), or (b) employing or engaging any person who responds to such a general solicitation or who approaches such party on an unsolicited basis.
